To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the configuration of advertising activities in multinational corporations is characterized by the location of responsibility for three broad sets of functions, strategic, executional, or evaluative, b) the location of these three sets of functions is either centralized at headquarters, or dispersed to the subsidiaries in the markets, with a few cases of both, and c) the coordination of advertising activities is done either at headquarters or at subsidiaries, but never by both.

the advertising functions of multinational corporations are managed in three broad sets, with each set managed either by headquarters or by subsidiaries and with very little evidence of coordination across the three sets.
multinational corporations' headquarters are involved in the strategic management of advertising and in the coordination of executional and evaluative advertising activities.

the configuration and coordination of advertising activities of large multinational firms, and the results of our research are summarized in the following paragraphs.
the configuration and coordination of global marketing activities.
the management of the advertising function in multinational companies and with the configuration and coordination of this function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the management of advertising activities by multinational corporations is a complex, multi-faceted, and dynamic process.
, in the area of advertising activities, multinational corporations are more likely to decentralize than to centralize.

the configuration of advertising activities within the multinational corporation is a function of a) the extent to which a particular function is strategic, b) the extent to that it is executional, c) the extent to the extent to which it is evaluative, and d) the extent to its complexity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the advertising activities of U.S. multinations are managed in a manner consistent with their overall organizational structures and the nature of their products.
multinational firms' advertising is managed by the headquarters in a centralized or decentralized fashion, and that coordination between headquarters and subsidiaries is not common.
the configuration of the advertising function in multinationals is a matter of trade-off between the benefits and costs of centralization and decentralization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multinational advertising management is not a monolithic activity.
multinational firms are not as centralized in advertising activities as is generally thought, and that there is considerable variation in their configuration and coordination across functions.
multinational firms are managing advertising in a way that is consistent with their overall management philosophy, which in turn is a reflection of the nature of the products they sell.
